references.text: Refers to wild animals that God sends as punishment, corresponding to 'the teeth of beasts' in Deuteronomy 32:24
Hunger as God's judgment on disobedience, parallel to 'wasted by famine' in the original text
Poisonous snakes sent as punishment, corresponding to 'the venom of crawling things' mentioned in the verse
Pestilence and disease as curses for breaking the covenant, parallel to pestilence and fever in Deuteronomy 32:24
Wild animals as part of God's four judgments, parallel to the teeth of wild beasts
Pestilence (reshef) mentioned as an attendant of God in judgment; the same Hebrew word is used
Pestilence and disease sent upon Egypt, using similar language for God's judgments
Pestilence that destroys at noonday, using the word 'qetev' (destruction) as in Deuteronomy 32:24
Sword, famine, pestilence, and wild animals as four instruments of punishment, corresponding to the four plagues in Moses' song
